# Problem Description

```{python}
#| label: problem-description-metrics
#| include: false

from pathlib import Path

import duckdb

trip_data_path = Path(
    "results/"
    "problem_description_trips.parquet"
)

problem_metrics = duckdb.sql(
    """
    WITH trips AS (
        SELECT
            trip_start_timestamp,
            pickup_community_area
        FROM read_parquet($trip_data_path)
    ),
    daily_demand AS (
        SELECT
            CAST(trip_start_timestamp AS DATE) AS trip_date,
            COUNT(*) AS trip_starts
        FROM trips
        GROUP BY trip_date
    ),
    hourly_demand AS (
        SELECT
            EXTRACT('hour' FROM trip_start_timestamp)::INTEGER AS hour,
            COUNT(*)::DOUBLE
                / COUNT(DISTINCT CAST(trip_start_timestamp AS DATE))
                AS average_trip_starts
        FROM trips
        GROUP BY hour
    ),
    area_demand AS (
        SELECT
            pickup_community_area,
            COUNT(*) AS trip_starts
        FROM trips
        WHERE pickup_community_area IS NOT NULL
        GROUP BY pickup_community_area
    ),
    ranked_areas AS (
        SELECT
            trip_starts,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY trip_starts DESC) AS demand_rank
        FROM area_demand
    )
    SELECT
        (SELECT SUM(trip_starts) FROM daily_demand) AS total_trip_starts,
        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM daily_demand) AS observed_days,
        (SELECT AVG(trip_starts) FROM daily_demand)
            AS average_daily_trip_starts,
        (
            SELECT 100.0 * SUM(trip_starts)
                / (SELECT SUM(trip_starts) FROM area_demand)
            FROM ranked_areas
            WHERE demand_rank <= 5
        ) AS top_five_area_share_pct,
        (
            SELECT hour
            FROM hourly_demand
            ORDER BY average_trip_starts DESC
            LIMIT 1
        ) AS peak_hour,
        (
            SELECT average_trip_starts
            FROM hourly_demand
            ORDER BY average_trip_starts DESC
            LIMIT 1
        ) AS peak_hour_average,
        (
            SELECT hour
            FROM hourly_demand
            ORDER BY average_trip_starts
            LIMIT 1
        ) AS low_hour,
        (
            SELECT average_trip_starts
            FROM hourly_demand
            ORDER BY average_trip_starts
            LIMIT 1
        ) AS low_hour_average
    """,
    params={"trip_data_path": str(trip_data_path)},
).df().iloc[0]

total_trip_starts = int(problem_metrics["total_trip_starts"])
observed_days = int(problem_metrics["observed_days"])
average_daily_trip_starts = problem_metrics["average_daily_trip_starts"]
top_five_area_share_pct = problem_metrics["top_five_area_share_pct"]
peak_hour = int(problem_metrics["peak_hour"])
peak_hour_average = problem_metrics["peak_hour_average"]
low_hour = int(problem_metrics["low_hour"])
low_hour_average = problem_metrics["low_hour_average"]
peak_to_low_ratio = peak_hour_average / low_hour_average
```

For operators of ride-hailing services tactical and strategical capabilities in operations mangement are a precondition 
for market success. On the one hand the operator needs to understand the dynamics of the market to make guided strategical
decisions, like in which cities and areas a ride-hailing business is likely profitable. On the other hand it is also crucial for
the operator to be able to make daily tactical decision, for example to predict where and when demand will be high. We have conducted an analysis of the taxi demand in Chicago, US to enable our customer to build the tactical and 
strategical capabilities. With a total of `{python} f"{total_trip_starts:,}"` started trips across `{python} f"{observed_days:,}"` days, and 
`{python} f"{average_daily_trip_starts:,.0f}"` average daily trip starts, we believe that the scope of our taxi demand anylsis in Chicago is a good enough proxy for ride-hailing operations.
The tactical and strategical capabilities involve business and data understanding, whereby data understanding can be seen 
as the foundation. Therefore the data mining goal is to describe the dynamics of the taxi market in Chicago and develop
prediction models to forecast demand. Further we evaluate whether these models are sufficient to make demand forecasting for daily operations.
The business goal is to argue whether a market entry in Chicago looks promising to our customer. Within this report we present the findings of our analysis.
